page: PDF p. 90 (book p. 66); repeated PDF p. 102 (book p. 78)
chapter: Ch. 4 — The Anatomy of an AI Workload
evidence: Canonical Workload box, PDF p. 90: "The modelled components are retrieval ~120 ms + prefill ~1.08 s + decode ~7.5 s = ~8.7 s, plus ~15% planning headroom to ~10 s."  PDF p. 102 (same chapter): "The 1.08 s prefill term inside Wexec is the two-term budget cap, not a modelled runtime (Table 4-2: TTFT 1.2 s − retrieval 120 ms, with zero allowance for admission/queue and tokenization/transfer)."  PDF p. 106: "The 1.08 s prefill figure is the two-term budget cap (TTFT 1.2 s − retrieval 120 ms; Table 4-2), not a modeled prefill runtime: the modeled host prefill is ~0.16 s at peak and ~0.47 s at 35% MFU (Ch 2), and only the budget-cap term enters the execution window used here."
issue: Within one chapter the 1.08 s prefill term is labelled a *modelled component* of service time in the Canonical Workload box (and again in the Arithmetic Walk-Through, PDF p. 102: "retrieval ~120 ms + prefill ~1.08 s + decode ~7.5 s ≈ 8.7 s"), while the same chapter states twice that it is a budget cap and explicitly *not* a modelled runtime (the modelled host prefill is ~0.47 s at 35% MFU). The 1.08 s budget cap is what builds Wexec ≈ 8.58 s → execution occupancy ~86/~344 → the 6-host average and 21-host peak fleets and every $/1K figure, so mislabelling it as a modelled runtime invites a reader to treat the cap as a measured duration.
fix_instruction: In the Canonical Workload box and the Arithmetic Walk-Through step 2, replace "The modelled components are ... prefill ~1.08 s ..." with wording that names the term as a budget cap (e.g. "budget-derived components: retrieval ~120 ms + prefill budget cap ~1.08 s + decode ~7.5 s"), matching Table 4-2's row label "two-term-only upper cap, NOT a feasible deployed prefill target". Keep the label set consistent across all six occurrences of the 1.08 s term.

chapter: Ch. 2 — What Actually Happens During Inference
evidence: §2.5 Common Mistakes: "Cross-technology numbers follow the same rule — name the SKU, not the memory class: the H200 (HBM3e successor to the H100) is 4.8 TB/s, B200-class HBM3e is ~8 TB/s, and AMD MI300X is ~5.3 TB/s [1P][FACT] — vendor-published specifications as of the 2026-08-30 cutoff; verify against the specific generation in use."
issue: Three vendor hardware constants carry the [1P][FACT] pair, but no first-party source is named for any of them ("vendor-published specifications" is generic). The book's own evidence discipline requires a named first-party source for [1P] — compare Table 4-2's rows "[1P][FACT] NVIDIA H100 SXM5 datasheet (80 GB HBM3)" and "[1P][FACT] NVIDIA H100 SXM5 datasheet (1,979 TFLOPS with sparsity ÷ 2)", and the Preface's "[1P] — first-party: the model vendor's own spec". These three figures are load-bearing in the surrounding argument that "The comparison to the 5.6 TB/s decode demand shifts the GPU count equation" (Ch. 2 §2.7), so their provenance must be checkable.
fix_instruction: Name the specific datasheet (or model card) behind each constant, e.g. "NVIDIA H200 SXM datasheet (HBM3e, 4.8 TB/s)", "NVIDIA B200 datasheet", "AMD Instinct MI300X datasheet", each with the access date, consistent with the Table 4-2 style; or downgrade the labels to [2°][DERIVED] if the figures are carried from a secondary summary.

chapter: Ch. 2 — What Actually Happens During Inference
evidence: §2.5 Common Mistakes: "H100 3.35 TB/s HBM3 is the theoretical peak; actual sustained bandwidth for weight-read kernels may be 60–80% of peak [HYPOTHESIS] — a rule of thumb, not measured or cited here."  The book's rule, Preface PDF p. 20 (book p. xvi): "Every load-bearing quantitative claim carries Axes 1 and 2 as an inline pair (e.g. [1P][DERIVED]); Axis 3, measurement status, rides along where a claim's status is known."
issue: A quantitative performance ratio (60–80% of peak) is tagged with Axis 2 only ([HYPOTHESIS]), with no Axis-1 provenance, violating the book's own two-axis label-pair rule for load-bearing quantitative claims. The same chapter applies the rule correctly elsewhere (e.g. "[canonical scenario][DERIVED]", "[1P][FACT]"), and the Preface states: "A label pair always takes one item from each of the first two axes." The figure is also reused as an analytical input in the same paragraph ("the same shard takes ~8.7–6.5 ms", PDF p. 54), so it carries downstream weight.
fix_instruction: Give the 60–80% figure a full pair — e.g. [2°][HYPOTHESIS] if it comes from an industry rule of thumb, or [canonical scenario][ASSUMPTION] if it is the book's own planning assumption — and add the Axis-3 status (MEASURED/UNMEASURED). If no provenance exists, remove the numeric range and state the qualitative point only.

evidence: Figure 6.2 axis annotation (rendered in-figure label): "SLO 2 s (TTFT budget)", with the shaded region labelled "SLO-violating region (> 2 s)" and the caption noting "the p95 TTFT ceiling (Table 4-2), not the 1.2 s design budget". Ch. 4 §4.3, PDF p. 106: "The two thresholds are not interchangeable: 1.2 s is the design budget, ≤ 2 s is the p95 ceiling the budget relaxes to, and any pass/fail judgement on a measured distribution is made against the p95 ceiling, not the budget."
issue: The figure's own in-figure label calls the 2 s line the "TTFT budget", while the book's defined TTFT budget is 1.2 s (1.2 s = retrieval ~120 ms + prefill ~1.08 s) and 2 s is only the p95 ceiling. The caption of the very same figure contradicts the label, and Ch. 4 §4.3 explicitly forbids conflating the two. A reader who reads only the plotted annotation (the rendered label) will mis-attribute the SLO line.
fix_instruction: Relabel the figure annotation from "SLO 2 s (TTFT budget)" to "p95 TTFT ceiling 2 s" (and keep the shaded band caption consistent), so that the in-figure text, the figure caption and Ch. 4 §4.3 use one term for each threshold.

page: PDF p. 27 (book p. 4); cross-refs at PDF p. 21 (Preface) and PDF pp. 62, 74 (Ch. 3)
chapter: Ch. 1 — It All Starts With the First Token (cross-reference form)
evidence: Ch. 1 §1.1.2, PDF p. 27: "... DeepSeek-V4 technical report, arXiv 2606.19348, and model card HF deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Pro — all accessed 2026-08-30, the book's evidence cutoff; A.10" and again "model card HF Qwen/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next, accessed 2026-08-30; A.10".  Preface, PDF p. 21: "Appendix A, A.6 carries a boxed 2026-09-27 capability probe ..." and "a superseding re-verification of the DeepSeek model-service status (Appendix A, A.3)".  Ch. 3, PDF p. 74: "is in Appendix A §9A, 'Noise-stage expert selection (Wan2.2 A14B)'"; PDF p. 62: "carried in Appendix A §9A (alternative inference in detail)".  Stated convention, Preface PDF p. 23: "Appendix A numbers its own sections with a letter suffix, so Appendix A § 9A means Appendix A, the section labelled 9A; the appendix's figures carry A.N."
issue: Three incompatible forms are used for the same class of reference: "A.10" and "A.6"/"A.3" (letter-dot-digit, used for appendix sections) and "§9A" (digit-then-letter, the form the Preface declares normative). "A.10" additionally collides with the appendix's figure numbering scheme (A.N per the Preface and the List of Figures, A.1–A.5), so a reader cannot tell whether it points at section 10A, figure A.10, or nothing — and no A.10 figure exists in the List of Figures.
fix_instruction: Normalise every appendix cross-reference to the declared convention ("Appendix A §10A", "Appendix A §6A", "Appendix A §3A", "Appendix A §9A"), reserving "A.N" exclusively for figures and tables. Sweep the whole book for the "A.N"-as-section form (it currently appears at least three times) and rewrite them.

chapter: Ch. 1 — It All Starts With the First Token
evidence: §1.1.2: "Current-gen models commonly ship windows ranging from roughly 8K tokens in older or small-tier deployments up to a million-plus tokens at the frontier, varying by model and vendor — for example, the Qwen3.8-Flash-Next card states a native 262K-token window with YaRN extension to 1M, and the GLM-5.3-Flash and DeepSeek-V4 cards state 1M [1P][FACT] ... ; the low end of that range is the older/edge tier rather than a published figure for a current frontier model [1P][HYPOTHESIS]."
issue: The [1P] provenance is applied to a statement that is the book's own market characterization ("the low end of that range is the older/edge tier rather than a published figure for a current frontier model"), not to anything a vendor published — the same paragraph's card-derived statements are correctly tagged [1P][FACT]. The book's own Axis-1 definition is "[1P] — first-party: the model vendor's own spec", and the Preface warns against provenance/status mismatch.
fix_instruction: Re-tag this clause so the provenance matches its origin — e.g. [2°][HYPOTHESIS] (second-hand survey of vendor line-ups) or [canonical scenario][HYPOTHESIS] — or restate it as an explicitly author-chosen framing without an [1P] provenance, keeping [1P][FACT] only for the card-stated windows.

chapter: Ch. 5 — From Workload to Model Selection
evidence: §5.3(a): "... ~186–371 ms if encoded on a single CPU core at ~30–60 GFLOP/s sustained (~200 GFLOP/s is the AVX-512 theoretical peak, not a sustained rate), but only ~1.1 ms on a ~10 TFLOP/s GPU, which is the basis the ~120 ms retrieval budget already assumes (vector search and reranking on a local GPU, Ch 4). On that basis the incremental cost stays well within the ~120 ms retrieval budget; single-core encoding fits only above ≈92.8 GFLOP/s sustained per core (11.14 GFLOP ÷ 0.12 s), beyond the typical sustained range (371 ms at 30 GFLOP/s vs 186 ms at 60 GFLOP/s) — conditional on measured single-core throughput."
issue: The sentence "the incremental cost stays well within the ~120 ms retrieval budget" is immediately contradicted by the figures in the same sentence for the CPU case (186–371 ms > 120 ms). The referent of "On that basis" is ambiguous: it can only mean the GPU figure (~1.1 ms), yet the following clause re-argues the CPU case, so the reader cannot tell which basis the claim is made on. The claim is also the hinge for the paragraph's conclusion that "the incremental cost stays well within the ~120 ms retrieval budget".
fix_instruction: Split the sentence and name the basis explicitly: "On a GPU (~1.1 ms at ~10 TFLOP/s) the incremental cost stays well within the ~120 ms retrieval budget; on a single CPU core it does not — 186–371 ms at 30–60 GFLOP/s — so single-core encoding fits only above ≈92.8 GFLOP/s sustained per core." Keep the numbers as they are; only the referents need to be disambiguated.

evidence: Ch. 4 §4.6, PDF p. 115: "That 17-slot ceiling is a per-host figure, and its binding limit is per-rank: an 80 GB rank runs 99.97% full at 17.5 slots (Ch 7, Technical note — per-rank fit: 17.5 GB weights + 54.48 GB KV + 8 GB runtime/NCCL = 79.98 GB of 80 GB), so the per-rank test — not this pool-level arithmetic — decides residency."  Ch. 7 introduction, PDF p. 154: "Per-rank fit is the binding test and is derived once, in §7.3's technical note; do not read an aggregate fill level as a per-rank allocation."
issue: Ch. 4 cites the 17-slot per-rank derivation as living in "Ch 7, Technical note", and Ch. 7's own introduction designates "§7.3's technical note" as its single home — but the cited derivation (17.5 GB weights + 54.48 GB KV + 8 GB runtime = 79.98 GB of 80 GB at 17.5 slots) does not appear anywhere in Ch. 7 §7.3; the only per-rank computation in §7.3 is the 128K-context row ("weights 17.5 + KV 41.94 + the full runtime-reserve share 64 ÷ 8 = 8 GB gives 67.4 GB ≤ 80 GB"). Ch. 7's intro therefore points to a derivation that is absent from the section it names, and Ch. 4's citation resolves only to itself.
fix_instruction: Either move the 17-slot per-rank fit into Ch. 7 §7.3 (as the labelled technical note Ch. 7's introduction promises) so both citations land on the same derivation, or change Ch. 4's reference to the section that actually contains it. In either case make the reference use the declared § form (Ch. 7 §3.3 / §7.3) rather than the free-text "Technical note".
